alex: Heads up — noticed repeated bursts of errorbudget burn in eu-west last 48h tied to GPU saturation. grafana shows node-level saturation spikes coincident with tenant tail-latency. anyone seen this pattern before?
jamie: Yep saw a couple of those. usually starts when smaller tenants flood with long sequences and continuous batching ramps.
nidhi: Can you paste the grafana panel link or the PromQL you used?
alex: Panel: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/abcd/gpu-fleet-overview
PromQL i looked at: `sum(rate(gpu_vram_utilization_bytes[2m])) / sum(gpu_total_vram_bytes) by (region)` and `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,tenant))`
ken: Two quick thoughts: 1) alerting granularity is too coarse — region-level burn hides tenant hotspots. 2) our current EB controller only uses error_rate/latency SLOs, not saturation.
sre-bot: Incident detected: eu-west GPU saturation alert x3 (2109876552) — linked runbook: /runbooks/gpu-saturation.md
jamie: We should consider a composite SLI that factors saturation (gpu_saturation_ratio) into burn calculations. otherwise day-to-day noisy saturation will eat errorbudget even if user-visible ops ok.
nidhi: +1. what would composite look like? maybe weight 70% latency, 30% saturation? also need to cap sensitivity so short spikes don't blow EB.
alex: Prototype idea: composite_sli = 0.7 * latency_ok + 0.3 * (1 - saturation_normalized)
ken: Also think about grouping alerts: short-lived saturation (under 3m) => warn, sustained (>=10m) => hard EB burn. Helps reduce noise.
ops-bot: Suggestion: route low-priority tenants to best-effort queue when composite_sli < 0.85 OR region saturation > 0.9.
jamie: We must be careful with routing — some tenants are latency-sensitive but classified low-cost. need tenant-priority matrix. propose tiers: platinum, gold, silver, best-effort.
nidhi: Agree. We should encode fallback policies in EB controller so rollbacks and automated mitigations are auditable. e.g. policy row: region, tenant_tier, trigger, mitigation, expected impact.
alex: Sketch of policy matrix (quick):
```
- region: eu-west
  tenant_tier: platinum
  trigger: composite_sli < 0.9 for >=5m
  mitigation: move to reserved pool in same region (if capacity) else fallback to dedicated in us-west
  expected_impact: <1% increased latency
- region: eu-west
  tenant_tier: silver
  trigger: composite_sli < 0.85 for >=3m
  mitigation: degrade model quantization -> 4-bit, move to best-effort pool
  expected_impact: quality drop, lower cost
```
jamie: That looks good. question: how do we measure expected impact? we need canary traffic to estimate latency delta and quality regression.
ken: We can use synthetic probe tenants (slo-probes) hitting representative prompts and store pre/post metrics in influx/grafana; tie regression alert to eval-set.
sre-bot: Reminder: add new composite_sli -> metric name `redwood_composite_sli` to metrics catalog.
ops-bot: For alerting tuning: propose two alerts: `SLOBurn:fast` (5m burn rate > 4x expected) and `SLOBurn:slow` (1h burn rate > 1.25x). fast = immediate oncall page, slow = pager to rotation if persists.
nidhi: And annotate dashboards with owner and runbook links so on-call can triage quickly.
alex: Action items: 1) jamie + ken: draft composite_sli promql & Grafana panel (due EOD Fri). 2) nidhi: start policy matrix doc and tenant tier sweep (due Mon). 3) ops-bot: add synthetic probe job for eu-west (dev run by Wed).
jamie: I'll throw initial PromQL here later but quick version: `avg_over_time((0.7 * (1 - (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,tenant)))) + 0.3 * (1 - clamp_max(sum(gpu_saturation_ratio) by (region),1))) [5m:1m])` — prototype, needs tuning.
ken: Let's also not forget cost implications: routing platinum to reserved may increase committed spend. include finance in policy review before enforcement.
nidhi: Good call. I'll loop in finance and product for approval path.
sre-bot: Noted — new EPIC created: SRE-4523 "Composite SLI + EB mitigation matrix"
alex: thanks all. let's sync in the weekly SRE sync Thurs 10am to review progress. :thumbsup:
